description: Cross-stack HWMON HEADER role-classification agreement vectors (AUD3-c, DEC-322). The daemon's hwmon::roles::classify_header_role + is_pump_protected and the GUI's services.pump_protection.header_is_pump_protected MUST agree on every case. This pins the classifier that decides whether the fan wizard offers to STOP a header, which is why it is a safety oracle and not a tidiness one: if the daemon learns a new pump-classifying label (/ofc:superio-curator exists to add exactly that) and the GUI's hand-mirrored copy does not, the GUI concludes 'not protected' and offers to stop a real pump. Inference only: every case has assigned = None, because a user assignment is runtime.toml state neither side infers. The GUI reconstruction is the FALLBACK path (a daemon >= 2.31.0 publishes stop_permitted and the GUI prefers it), so these cases are driven with stop_permitted = null. is_aio is an INPUT for the GUI, which cannot see chip_name; the daemon derives it from chip_name via aio::is_liquid_cooler_chip and the daemon test asserts that derivation too, so the field cannot drift from the chip list. This file must be byte-identical in both repos (daemon/tests/fixtures and the GUI tests/fixtures) and is gated by parity.yml.

cases.name: synthesised_placeholder_channel_1
cases.why: DEC-229: a synthesised pwmN restates the channel index and is not evidence. This is the it8696 AIO-MB validation target, which publishes no label files at all.
cases.label: pwm1

cases.name: synthesised_placeholder_channel_5
cases.why: Same rule at the other end of the it8696's five channels.
cases.label: pwm5

cases.name: placeholder_rule_is_index_specific
cases.why: 'pwm2' on channel 1 is NOT the placeholder for that channel, so it counts as a real (unrecognised) label. Both sides must key the placeholder test on the channel index, not on the pwm-prefix alone.
cases.label: pwm2

cases.name: pump_hint_outranks_a_chassis_hint
cases.why: SYS_FAN5_PUMP carries both a chassis hint and a pump hint. The pump reading must win on both sides — a false positive floors a fan, a false negative stops a pump.
cases.label: SYS_FAN5_PUMP

cases.name: cpu_fan_hyphen_normalises
cases.why: Both sides normalise '-', ' ' and '.' to '_' before matching.
cases.label: CPU-FAN

cases.name: cpu_opt_is_deliberately_ambiguous
cases.why: CPU_OPT is the header the AIO brief forbids guessing: it is as often a pump as a second CPU fan. It must classify as unknown, NOT cpu_fan, on both sides.
cases.label: CPU_OPT

cases.name: cooler_channel_1_is_the_pump
cases.why: Chip mapping: on a known liquid cooler, channel 1 is the pump. Verified against nzxt-kraken3 (pwm1=pump, pwm2=fan).

cases.name: cooler_placeholder_still_reaches_chip_mapping
cases.why: Skipping the synthesised label is what LETS the chip mapping run on a cooler that publishes no label files.
cases.label: pwm1

cases.name: a_label_outranks_the_chip_mapping
cases.why: THE load-bearing precedence case. A cooler's channel 1 labelled CPU_FAN1 is a CPU fan, not a pump: a label is direct per-channel evidence while chip mapping is a positional assumption. Getting this backwards on one side only is how the two classifiers would diverge in the unsafe direction.
cases.label: CPU_FAN1

cases.name: a_pump_label_on_a_cooler_channel_2_still_wins
cases.why: A dual-pump loop: pwm2 labelled PUMP classifies Pump under label-first and RadiatorFan under mapping-first, and only one of those refuses to stop it.
cases.label: PUMP
